chapter: Tiny Bradshaw, Teddy Hill and Europe
title: Touring with Tiny Bradshaw to Chicago and Ohio
summary: Procope recalls Tiny Bradshaw as a fun leader with a jazz band of shouts, stomps and blues; they played the Harlem Opera House, the Regal in Chicago and Ohio dates for about three months.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: All right, now back to Tiny Bradshaw.

Oh, Tiny Bradshaw, oh, yes. I liked Tiny. Tiny was a -- he was a good kid. He was a sort of a drummer. He wasn't a great or even a good drummer, and by the time I joined his band and went to Chicago, he was just directing the band. And he could dance and sing and sort of a takeoff on Cab Calloway type of thing, and I had -- then again I say I had -- I had a good time in Tiny's band, because he was a fun guy. He liked to have a good time and he liked automobiles, he liked cars, you know, he liked to drive and that sort of thing. And I got to do pretty much in his band like I wanted to do, you know. I'd say, hey, man , so and so
and so, and he'd get the music, you know, and I could work out on it on my clarinet. That sort of thing.
Well, what sort of music was he playing then? In '34. It later became sort of a rhythm and blues, jump band.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, he had a jazz band. He had a jazz band. Played all the shouts, we used to call them. The shouts and the stomps and the --
Right.
-- blues. He could sing the blues, you know. And he played ballads. He had a good setup, a good setup.
Where did you work?
Oh, we played theaters. We didn't play the Apollo. We played the other theater down the street, the M&S, they used to call it. Remember the other theater on 125th Street and 8th Avenue? Shows too.
(Inaudible)
Yes. There was a theater on the same side of the street as the Apollo, down towards 7th Avenue, about -- you know, about a quarter of the way up in the lot.
On the same side as the Apollo.
Yes.
That's now a movie house?
No. That was Loew's Victoria.
Oh, yeah.
That was a Loew's theater. It was an old vaudeville house way back, you know, in the old days. We used to call it the M&S.
Uh-huh.
I can't think now -- the Harlem Opera House.
Oh, the Harlem Opera House.

The Harlem Opera House I'm talking about. The Harlem Opera House, yeah. That was the theater we played with Tiny. I didn't stay with Tiny long. We made a trip to Chicago and, you know, every once in awhile you want to go somewhere, and it was just for a short time, so I took the gig and we went to Chicago and played the Regal Theater, and we had some dates in Ohio, like that, and Tiny's home was in Ohio and we played his hometown, some small town in Ohio, and I think it lasted about three months, two or three months, something like that. Not long.
